name: apicircle-vscode
description: Git-backed API workspace with mocks, plans, and MCP — natively in VS Code.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No workspace active.

Open a folder with `.apicircle/workspace.json` or create a new workspace to get started.

[Create New Workspace](command:apicircle.createWorkspace)
[Open Folder…](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

Welcome to API Circle Studio.

API Circle keeps your API workspace in a Git-friendly file at `.apicircle/workspace.json`, so you can edit it here, in the desktop app, or in the web app — all on the same repo.

No `.apicircle/workspace.json` was found in the open folder. Create one or open a folder that already has one.

[Create New Workspace](command:apicircle.createWorkspace)
[Open Folder…](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)

Your API Circle workspace is ready.

[Open workspace.json](command:apicircle.openWorkspaceFile) to inspect the underlying Git-tracked file, or create your first request to start sending.

[New Request](command:apicircle.newRequest)
[New Request from Template…](command:apicircle.newRequestFromTemplate)

Environments hold variables (`{{base_url}}`, secrets, …) you reference from requests.

[New Environment](command:apicircle.newEnvironment)
[Set Active Environment](command:apicircle.setActiveEnvironment)
[Set Priority Order…](command:apicircle.setEnvPriorityOrder)

Execution plans chain requests with assertions to validate end-to-end flows.

[New Plan](command:apicircle.newPlan)

No mock servers yet.

Mock servers spin up local HTTP endpoints from OpenAPI / Postman / Insomnia specs (or a manual endpoint list). Start them with ▶ Start, stop with ■ Stop — they live until VS Code closes.

[New Mock…](command:apicircle.newMock)

Recent request and plan runs land here as you ▶ Send / Run.

No runs yet — send a request from the Editor view to populate this list.

No snapshots yet.

Workspace snapshots are point-in-time copies of `synced` state. Use them to undo accidental deletes or revert before risky imports — the safety net for Git-tracked workspace changes.

[Capture Snapshot…](command:apicircle.captureSnapshot)
[Set Storage Cap…](command:apicircle.setSnapshotMaxBytes)

MCP integration exposes your workspace to Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Continue, Cline, Zed, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and ChatGPT.

Open a folder with `.apicircle/workspace.json` to see per-AI-client config snippets you can paste into each client.

[Open Connect Guide](command:apicircle.openMcpConnectGuide)

Open a folder with `.apicircle/workspace.json` to manage this workspace's releases — the versions linked consumers pin to.

[Create New Workspace](command:apicircle.createWorkspace)

No releases published yet.

Publish a version to give linked consumers something to pin to. Each release is fingerprinted with a SHA-256 of the workspace contents.

[Publish release…](command:apicircle.publishRelease)
[Open release history](command:apicircle.openReleaseHistory)

Or discover and link workspaces from the marketplace:

[Search Marketplace…](command:apicircle.searchMarketplace)
[Link a Workspace…](command:apicircle.linkWorkspace)

apicircle.execution.host.description: Whether localhost executes against the extension host (typical) or tunnels to the user's machine via VS Code port forwarding (Remote-SSH / Codespaces only).

apicircle.execution.timeoutMs.description: Hard timeout in milliseconds for a single request send.

apicircle.history.retentionDays.description: Days to retain request and plan run history.

apicircle.history.maxEntriesPerWorkspace.description: Max history entries kept per workspace before oldest are evicted.

apicircle.mock.defaultPort.description: Default port when starting a mock server (null = pick a free port).

apicircle.mcp.autoConfigureClients.markdownDescription: **(Phase 8 + 11)** List of AI clients to target when the **Install MCP for All Configured Clients** command runs. Each entry tells APICircle to merge an `apicircle` MCP server entry into that client's user-level config file (e.g. `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, `~/.continue/config.yaml`). Empty by default — the bulk command prompts you with a multi-pick if no clients are configured. Supported: `claude-desktop`, `claude-code`, `cursor`, `windsurf`, `zed`, and (Phase 11) `continue` (YAML config). Cline is not auto-configurable — it reads workspace `.vscode/mcp.json` so use **Install for Copilot Chat / VS Code MCP** instead.

apicircle.mcp.allowDecrypt.markdownDescription: **(Phase 6+ — deferred)** When true, MCP tools may receive decrypted secret values from the active workspace's vault. Off by default for safety — today MCP clients only see encrypted `enc:v1:` wires. Requires the vault to be unlocked. Wiring this means the security model has to gate per-tool access — that work lands in Phase 6 alongside the in-extension MCP host.

enumDescriptions: Open APICircle files as YAML text (recommended).
Open APICircle files in the visual editor by default.
Open YAML and visual editors side-by-side automatically.
apicircle.editor.defaultView.markdownDescription: **(Phase 6+ — deferred)** Default editor view for APICircle YAML files. The visual editor lands as part of the Phase 6 opt-in webview workstream; until then the extension is all-native YAML.

apicircle.secrets.autoLockMinutes.markdownDescription: Auto-lock the secret vault after this many minutes of inactivity. `0` = never auto-lock. Changes take effect immediately for already-unlocked vaults.

apicircle.secrets.clipboardClearSeconds.markdownDescription: Clear a revealed secret from the clipboard after this many seconds. `0` = never clear. The clipboard is only cleared if it still holds the value that was copied (you can paste freely without the timer wiping the buffer).

apicircle.secrets.rememberOnDevice.markdownDescription: **(Phase 8)** Remember the vault passphrase on this device via VS Code's SecretStorage (backed by OS keychain — Keychain on macOS, Credential Manager on Windows, libsecret on Linux). When enabled, after a successful unlock the passphrase is persisted; the next time you open the workspace the vault unlocks silently. **Security tradeoff:** anyone with access to your OS keychain can read the passphrase, so this should only be enabled on a trusted, encrypted-at-rest device. Disabled by default. Use the **APICircle: Forget Vault Credentials on This Device** command to wipe the stored entry.

apicircle.mcp.embeddedHost.enabled.markdownDescription: **(Phase 10)** Run an in-extension MCP server over Streamable HTTP. When enabled, the extension exposes the 78-tool MCP catalog on a local loopback port that AI clients (Copilot Chat, Cursor, Claude Desktop with the HTTP transport) can connect to directly — no separate `apicircle-mcp` binary required. Off by default. **Security:** binds ONLY to loopback (`127.0.0.1` / `::1`); bearer-token auth on every request; DNS-rebinding protection via Host-header validation; token rotates on every **Restart**. Use **APICircle: Copy Embedded MCP Host URL** to share the connection URL (incl. token) with your AI client.

apicircle.mcp.embeddedHost.port.markdownDescription: **(Phase 10)** Port the embedded MCP host binds to. `0` = let the OS pick a free port (recommended, the chosen port is shown in the MCP view). Set explicitly if you've pre-configured your AI client with a fixed port.

apicircle.mcp.embeddedHost.bindHost.markdownDescription: **(Phase 10)** Host interface the embedded MCP host binds to. **Must be a loopback address** (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `::1`, or any `127.x.y.z`). Any non-loopback value is rejected at startup — binding to a non-loopback interface would expose the workspace's MCP tools to the network and is never safe.

apicircle.mcp.binaryPath.markdownDescription: Path to the `apicircle-mcp` binary that external AI clients launch as their MCP server. Defaults to `apicircle-mcp` (assumes the binary is on `PATH`, installed via `pnpm install -g @apicircle/mcp-server`). Set to an absolute path if you installed the binary in a non-standard location.

apicircle.mcp.workspaceConfigPath.markdownDescription: Path (relative to the workspace folder) where the **Install for Copilot Chat / VS Code MCP** command writes the workspace-level MCP config. Default `.vscode/mcp.json` is the standard location VS Code 1.86+ Copilot Chat reads automatically. Override only if your project uses a non-standard location.

apicircle.validation.validateOnSend.description: Run pre-send validation before every send.
